lessons.title: Describing a recent problem
objectives: Give a simple account of a recent health or service problem.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about explaining a headache.

content_sections.title: Notice form and meaning (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read the model aloud twice: 'I have had a headache since yesterday, so I need some advice.' Underline the words that show the situation, time, or result. In this lesson, give a simple account of a recent health or service problem. Keep the language connected: do not give isolated words.

content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about explaining a headache. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Give a simple account of a recent health or service problem.

content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)
content_sections.body: Create a short message about explaining a headache without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.

exercises.prompt: Choose the response that gives a clear, useful message for this situation: explaining a headache.
options: I have had a headache since yesterday, so I need some advice.
The bus stopped at River Road, and the driver explained the delay.
I am going to start early, but I will message you if the bus is late.
exercises.correct_answer: I have had a headache since yesterday, so I need some advice.

exercises.prompt: Complete the model with the missing words: 'I have had a headache since yesterday, so I ____.'
Read this short message for the lesson 'Describing a recent problem' and identify the real-life situation it describes.
exercises.stimulus: I have had a headache since yesterday, so I need some advice. The message gives one main point and one detail for the listener.

questions.question: What situation does the message describe?
acceptable_answers: The message is about explaining a headache.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 30–45 seconds about explaining a headache. State the main message, add a relevant detail, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Communicates the main message about explaining a headache clearly.
Adds a relevant detail and responds appropriately to a follow-up question.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about explaining a headache. Answer the question before the transcript is revealed, then listen again and check the key detail.
listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about explaining a headache.
listening.transcript: I have had a headache since yesterday, so I need some advice.
listening.question: What is the message mainly about?
listening.answer: The listener should understand that it concerns explaining a headache.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay explaining a headache. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about explaining a headache.
constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.

pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for explaining a headache in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in explaining a headache easy to hear.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in describing a recent problem
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about explaining a headache. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about explaining a headache.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.

lessons.title: Review: health and services
objectives: Review the unit language in a short problem-and-response exchange.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about reviewing a health problem.

content_sections.title: Recall and select (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work without notes first. For the situation 'reviewing a health problem', say one sentence that meets this goal: Review the unit language in a short problem-and-response exchange. Then check the model: 'I described the problem clearly, asked for advice, and wrote down the next step.' Identify one word or phrase that makes the message clear.

content_sections.title: Compare two responses (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Give one clear response for reviewing a health problem, then ask a partner one follow-up question. Compare the response with the model and repair one missing time, reason, place, quantity, or next step. Use the whole unit's familiar language rather than memorising one sentence.

content_sections.title: Self-check and transfer (6 minutes)
content_sections.body: Before the unit test, check three things: the main message is clear, one useful detail is included, and the listener knows what happens next. Say or write a new short message about a similar situation, not the model about reviewing a health problem.
